content.title: Разные билеты
content.story:
Ира и Миша пришли на вокзал. Они хотели ехать вместе в Тулу. У Иры был билет в Тулу. Она купила его вчера. У Миши тоже был билет. Но он посмотрел на билет и сказал:
— Ира, мой поезд едет в Москву. Это другой город.
Ира взяла его билет. На билете было написано: «Москва».
— Миша, ты купил билет не в тот город, — сказала Ира.
До поезда было двадцать минут. Друзья посмотрели на табло. Потом они пошли к кассе. У кассы стояли люди.
— Что нам делать? — спросил Миша.
Ира посмотрела на него.
— Давай спросим кассира. Может быть, билет ещё можно поменять.
Друзья подошли к окну кассы.

glossary.meaning: and; joins people or ideas.
they; refers here to Ira and Misha.
to arrive; «пришли» is past tense, plural.
to the railway station; «на» with the accusative marks a destination.
to want; «хотели» is past tense, plural.
to travel by vehicle; «едет» means is going.
together; with one another.
to; with the accusative, marks a destination.
Tula, a city; «Тулу» is the destination form.
at someone’s place; in «у Иры был билет», introduces what someone has.
to be; «был» and «было» are past forms used here with different grammatical genders.
ticket; «билете» is the form used after «на».
yesterday; the day before today.
she; refers here to Ira.
to buy; «купила» is past tense feminine, «купил» past tense masculine.
it; refers to the ticket in «купила его».
he; refers here to Misha.
also; indicates that something is true for Misha as well.
but; introduces a contrast.
to look; «посмотрел», «посмотрела» and «посмотрели» are past-tense forms.
at, onto; marks what someone looks at or takes.
to say; «сказал» and «сказала» are past-tense forms.
my; shows that the train belongs with or is assigned to the speaker.
train; the vehicle the friends plan to travel on.
Moscow; «в Москву» means to Moscow.
this; points out or identifies something.
different; not the same one.
city; «город» is the direct form and «города» follows «другой».
to take; «взяла» is past tense feminine.
to write; in «было написано», means that something was written or said in writing.
it said on the ticket; a common way to describe written information.
you; informal singular form.
not to the right city; «тот» means the one intended or expected.
to say; «сказала» reports what Ira said.
until; marks how much time remains before an event.
twenty; the number 20.
minute; «минут» is the plural form used after двадцать.
friend; «друзья» means friends.
station display board; shows travel information such as trains.
then; after that.
to go on foot; «пошли» is past tense, plural.
to, toward; marks the person or place someone approaches.
ticket office or ticket counter; «кассе» and «кассы» are forms used after «к» and «у».
to stand; «стояли» is past tense, plural.
people; more than one person.
what; asks for information about a thing or action.
to us; the form of «мы» used here with «делать».
to do; asks what action they should take.
to ask; «спросил» is past tense masculine, «спросим» means we will ask.
him; after «на», refers to Misha in «посмотрела на него».
let’s; introduces a suggestion to do something together.
ticket clerk; the person at the ticket office who can help with tickets.
maybe; expresses that something is possible but uncertain.
still; indicates that changing the ticket may remain possible.
can; it is possible or permitted to do something.
to change or exchange; here, to get a different ticket.
to approach; «подошли» is past tense, plural.
window; «к окну» means toward the window.

content.title: Два билета
content.story:
Анна и Иван на вокзале. Они стоят рядом. У Анны есть сумка. У Ивана есть рюкзак.

— У меня есть билет, — говорит Анна. — А у тебя?

— У меня тоже есть билет, — говорит Иван.

Анна смотрит на часы.

— Наш поезд скоро. Где твой билет?

Иван достаёт билет из рюкзака. Анна достаёт свой билет из сумки. Друзья смотрят на билеты.

— Я еду в Москву, — говорит Анна. — Вот мой билет. Здесь написано: «Москва».

Иван смотрит на свой билет.

— А здесь написано: «Казань». Я еду в Казань?

Анна читает билет Ивана.

— Да, в Казань. Это другой город.

— Но мы едем вместе! — говорит Иван.

Анна кладёт два билета рядом.

— Смотри. У меня билет в Москву. У тебя билет в Казань.

Иван ещё раз читает билеты.

— У нас разные билеты, — говорит он.

— Да. И разные поезда, — говорит Анна.

Друзья смотрят друг на друга. Потом Иван смотрит на часы.

— Что мы теперь будем делать?

glossary.meaning: And; joins people or statements.
At the railway station; на takes the prepositional case here.
They; refers to Anna and Ivan.
To stand; стоят means ‘they are standing.’
Next to each other or side by side.
A way to say someone has something; the person after у is in the genitive case.
A bag; сумки is the genitive form used after из (‘out of’).
A backpack; рюкзака is the genitive form used after из (‘out of’).
A ticket; билеты and билета refer to more than one ticket here.
To say or speak; говорит means ‘says.’
And or but; introduces a comparison or a contrasting detail here.
You have; А у тебя? means ‘And do you have one?’
Also; Ivan has a ticket too.
To look at something; смотрит is singular and смотрят is plural.
A watch or clock used to check the time; this noun has a plural form.
Our; describes the train the friends expect to take.
A train; поезда is plural here.
Soon; their train is due soon.
Where; asks where Ivan’s ticket is.
Your; used when speaking to one person informally.
To take something out; достаёт means ‘takes out.’
Out of or from; followed by the genitive case.
One’s own; refers to the ticket belonging to the person doing the action.
A friend; друзья means ‘friends.’
I; the person speaking.
To travel by transport; еду means ‘I am going’ and едем means ‘we are going.’
To; introduces a destination and takes the accusative case here.
Here is; used to show someone a ticket.
My; describes Anna’s ticket.
Here; on this ticket.
Is written; introduces the destination printed on the ticket.
To read; читает means ‘reads.’
Yes; confirms the destination or the difference between the tickets.
This or that; points to the destination just mentioned.
Another or different; Kazan is not the same city as Moscow.
A city.
But; introduces Ivan’s objection.
We; the speaker and the other friend.
Together; travelling with each other.
To put or place; кладёт means ‘puts down.’
Two; followed by билета rather than билеты.
To look; Смотри is an informal command to one person: ‘Look.’
Once more; again.
We have; literally describes something belonging to us.
Different; разные describes the friends’ tickets and trains.
He; refers to Ivan.
At each other; the friends look at one another.
Then; introduces the next action.
What; asks what action they will take.
Now; after discovering the problem.
Will do or are going to do; будем plus the infinitive forms the future for ‘we.’

materialIssues: «город» — The note incorrectly says «города» follows «другой». The story correctly uses «другой город»; adjective agreement does not require «города». The forms list also repeats «город».

«на» — The explanation ‘marks what someone looks at or takes’ is misleading: taking the ticket in «Ира взяла его билет» does not involve «на». Here, distinguish looking at something from the location expressed by «на билете».
«у» — ‘At someone’s place’ does not explain «У кассы», which means at or near the ticket counter. The possession explanation for «У Иры был билет» is appropriate.
«его» — The notes explain the object pronouns in «купила его» and «на него», but not the possessive meaning ‘his’ in «его билет». These uses should be distinguished.

«Что нам делать?» and «На билете было написано» — The dative-plus-infinitive question and impersonal passive construction add grammatical load beyond the guide’s preference for explicit subjects and simple clauses. Phrase definitions help, but do not fully explain these structures.

«ты купил билет не в тот город» — Understandable, but «не в тот город» requires interpreting an intended destination rather than merely recognizing a concrete city name. Combined with several past-tense motion verbs, this makes the scene relatively demanding for the supplied A1 guide.
«сказать» — Two separate notes repeat the explanation of «сказала» without adding a distinct contextual meaning.
strengths: The intended shared destination and mistaken ticket are established clearly.
Most notes accurately explain contextual meanings and encountered verb forms.
Approaching the ticket counter creates a natural unresolved next step.

materialIssues: «Наш поезд скоро» — Understandable conversational ellipsis, but less idiomatic and less explicit for beginners than «Наш поезд скоро отправляется». This is a phrasing preference, not a case or agreement error.
«Анна кладёт два билета рядом» — The action is grammatically correct, but no surface is established. Naming where she puts the tickets would make the physical scene clearer.

«написано», «друг на друга» and «Что мы теперь будем делать?» — The impersonal passive form, reciprocal expression and compound future introduce additional grammatical load. Their notes provide useful support, though «написано» could explain its impersonal use more clearly.

«билет» — The explanation correctly identifies multiple tickets contextually, but could distinguish plural «билеты» from genitive singular «билета» after «два». The separate «два» note gives the correct combination without naming the form.
strengths: Short present-tense clauses, explicit subjects and repeated destination contrasts closely follow the guide.
Notes accurately support possession, reflexive «свой», case after prepositions and the command «Смотри».
The final question leaves a clear, natural unresolved problem rather than abruptly abandoning the scene.
